lines.line: Young or old, we expect little change ahead. Researchers call this an illusion.
Every body has hard days. The wise expect them, and stay calm.
lines.credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 627, tr. G. U. Pope

lines.line: A climber called Grandma Whitney took up jogging. Why? It made climbing much easier.
So pack before you go. Out for a day? Take bread for a week.
First in the bag, a strong body. The mind cannot carry the load alone.
lines.credit: Montaigne · Of the Education of Children

lines.line: Next, a breath habit: slow, deep and steady, until the mind finds balance.
And a mind like a mirror: it meets everything and holds on to nothing.
lines.credit: Zhuangzi · ch. 7, tr. H. A. Giles, 1889

lines.line: But stored bread is not eaten bread. Only what you practise becomes you.
So practise every day. Busy? Do one asana. But never skip completely.
Your daily bread: Ashtanga. Asana for strength, breath for lightness, turning inward for calm.
lines.credit: Gheranda Samhita 1.10-11 · tr. S. C. Vasu

lines.line: Every day brings hidden gifts. Leave them unused, and it quietly takes them back.
lines.credit: Ralph Waldo Emerson · Works and Days, 1870

lines.line: We want to know what's inside. But it's all uncertain. So, be patient.
lines.credit: Ajahn Chah · Not Sure!, Dhamma talk

lines.line: Patient, not idle: young Iyengar began yoga to grow strong for life's challenges.
lines.credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Life, 2005

lines.line: The body needs a little work each day, never too tiring, never forced.
lines.credit: Quoted by Sun Simiao · Qianjin Yaofang, c. 652

lines.line: And after 40, a more flexible body went with more flexible blood vessels.
lines.credit: Yamamoto et al. · Am J Physiol, 2009

lines.line: Not proud in success, not crushed in defeat. Whatever comes, never lose heart.
Daily 13-minute meditation eased bad moods and sharpened focus, but only after 8 weeks.
lines.credit: Basso et al., NYU · Behav Brain Res, 2019

lines.line: Musicians say: skip practice one day, you notice. Skip three, everyone notices.
And years of steady yoga, it is said, build an unshakable mind.
lines.credit: William James · The Energies of Men, 1907

lines.line: Shaping each day is the highest art. Open tomorrow's gifts on your Ashtanga mat.
Even Kipchoge tested his shoes in Kenya, yet had bad luck on race day.
Still, the body is built for this: it stays steady by adjusting to change.
So in Thailand we say: going into the forest? Don't forget your bush knife.
lines.credit: Thai saying · เข้าเถื่อนอย่าลืมพร้า

lines.line: Sharpen daily: one small hard thing, so the day of need finds you trained.
What does yoga give first? Lightness, health, steadiness, a bright face, a clear voice.
Fitness went with a steadier heart under stress, and a faster return to calm.
When trouble comes, smile with a patient, hopeful heart. Nothing has more power.
lines.credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 621, tr. G. U. Pope

lines.line: Sax player Sonny Rollins practised for hours every day. Cold? He played in gloves.
Nasagra drishti, the nose-tip gaze, kept up for months, helps steady a wandering mind.
Karate isn't only in the dojo. Your morning Ashtanga goes with you all day.
The alarm rings. What will today bring? Nobody knows. So start living now.
lines.credit: Seneca · On the Shortness of Life 9.1

lines.line: And live ready: the wise look ahead, so trouble cannot shake them.
lines.credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 429, tr. G. U. Pope

lines.line: How? Dancer Twyla Tharp's ritual wasn't the workout. It was getting into the taxi.
Two short, heavy lifting sessions a week improved weak bones in older women.
Eat just enough, keep regular hours, never overdo it: body and spirit stay together.
Relaxed face, calm full breath, soft muscles: where could tomorrow's worries get in?
lines.credit: William James · The Gospel of Relaxation

lines.line: Ayurveda's alarm clock: a healthy person rises before dawn, to protect a long life.
Then the same asanas daily: what felt impossible on Monday is normal by Saturday.
Train at a fixed hour, hot or cold, even when you'd rather not.
Set the alarm: regular practice eases stiffness, and morning practice helps you work better.
lines.credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966
